title: Goodfire monitors AI agents by reading signals inside the model
friendlyTitle: Goodfire watches what an AI model is doing inside
summary: Goodfire has launched internal-activation monitors for Kimi K3 deployments hosted by Baseten. Small probes watch model signals for risks such as offensive hacking or reward manipulation, then call a separate reviewer model only when something appears suspicious; company tests reported lower monitoring costs and modest latency overhead.
friendlySummary: Goodfire’s new monitors look at internal model signals while an agent works. A second AI checks the session only when the small monitor sees a possible risk.
whyItMatters: Continuous oversight can become expensive when agents work for hours, so cheaper monitoring may make controls practical for more deployments. The published detection and false-alarm figures are vendor tests on one model, however, and should not be treated as proof that an agent is safe.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This may make long-running agents cheaper to supervise. It is one safety layer, not a guarantee that the agent cannot cause harm.
